title: Siltvelt
text: “Is that so?”

“Siltvelt is a country that worships the Shield Hero, who favors Demi-Humans; therefore, the Shield Religion is the state religion. Since Lord Iwatani holds a position equivalent to that god’s, you see.”
My father shifts his gaze to me with a puzzled expression.
“What’s the matter?”
“Well, I was just wondering if you might know something about it, Motoyasu.”
“Even so, I haven’t heard anything about my future Father ever coming to this country.”
“Oh, is that so?”

That’s right. As far as I know, the number of countries my Father has visited can be counted on one hand. First, Melromarc, Zeltoble, Faubrey, and a few small nations neighboring Melromarc. Other than that, perhaps just the country where the battle against the Phoenix took place?

……Huh? I’m supposed to have fought the Phoenix, but my memory’s a bit fuzzy. If I hadn’t fought the Phoenix, I wouldn’t have fought the Qilin that appeared in Faubrey. Above all, there’s no way I could have performed the twelve enhancements of the Four Holy Weapons and the Seven Star Weapons. Huh? 4 plus 7 equals 11? Hmm, it seems there’s some sort of gap in my memory.
“According to Lord Kitamura, you were basically active within Melromarc, weren’t you? I hear you inherited my father’s territory there and successfully rebuilt it…”
“That is correct.”

“I do hope you’ll follow the same path in the future, but I’ve heard that path is fraught with hardship… I cannot let Lord Iwatani walk such a path. In that case, I wish to take on the task of rebuilding the territory myself.”
“Ms. Éclair… Yeah. You can do it, Ms. Éclair.”
“It’s reassuring to hear you say that, Lord Iwatani. I wish to prepare for the coming tide as soon as possible, and once peace returns to the world, I hope to rule my own domain.”
Éclair gazed up at the distant sky with eyes full of determination.

And so, we arrived at the castle of Siltvelt. As for the castle’s architecture… well, it’s hard to describe. It has a Chinese-style feel to it, yet it also features stonework with a medieval flair. The castle in Melromarc was reasonably large and tall, but this one is every bit as impressive. However, the doors, gates, and bridges all give the impression of being rather large, and vines are growing here and there. There are also many Beastmen, so if I had to describe it, it gives off a rather wild impression.
“Well, well, Shield Hero, Spear Hero, thank you for your hard work on this long journey.”
Upon arriving at the castle, we were escorted to the throne room.
“I am Werner, the representative of the Shusaku race. It’s a pleasure to make your acquaintance.”

The Shusaku race… I seem to recall hearing that they’re a famous race among the Demi-Humans. Hakuko, Shusaku, Aotatsu, and Genmu, was it? I believe there was someone called the Hakuko race under my future Father’s command… but I haven’t heard the details. I only know what they look like.
“N-nice to meet you… I’m Naofumi Iwatani, summoned as the Shield Hero. Nice to meet you.”
“The Love Hunter! I’m Motoyasu Kitamura!”
“Motoyasu, if you don’t declare yourself the Spear Hero, people will get the wrong idea, you know?”
“Is that so? Then, the Spear Hero, I guess.”
“What do you mean, ‘I guess’!?”
The Shusaku man looks completely taken aback.
“Nice to meet you. And…”
The Shusaku man shifts his gaze to Éclair.
“I take it you are the young lady of the Seaetto family.”
“Ah! My name is Eclair Seaetto. In place of my late father, I served as the bodyguard for the Shield Hero.”
“This arduous journey was a noble cause. I am truly grateful that you risked your own life to put a stop to the discrimination against Demi-Humans within the Kingdom of Melromarc.”
“No, I was merely doing my duty.”

Éclair bowed deeply. I don’t know the details, but I’d heard that Melromarc was a country that ruthlessly exploited Demi-Humans as slaves. However, I’ve heard that thanks to Father’s efforts and Éclair’s father’s great achievements, they’d managed to establish friendly relations with the Demi-Human nations.
“Hey, Naofumi, Sakura’s bored.”
“Sakura-chan, please be patient just a little longer.”
“Okay!”
My Father and Sakura-chan are having a warm conversation.
“Are those people companions who joined you along the way?”
“Um…”
“They’re Filolial-sama!”
Since my Father hesitated, I stepped forward and declared it. I, Motoyasu, simply cannot tolerate any misunderstanding on this point.
“Huh? Filolial-sama?”
“Yes. We’ve confirmed it with our own eyes. Until we entered our castle, these beings were Filolial-sama… taking the form of the divine birds from legend.”
“Come on, everyone! Show them what you’re made of!”
At my command, Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan made a “puff” sound as they transformed into their Filolial forms. Upon seeing them, the Shusaku man took a step back.
“I-I see… It’s reassuring to know the legendary Filolial are here.”
“So, does that mean we should stay in this country and prepare for the wave?”
Father moved on to the main topic.
“Before that, we were just thinking we’d let you rest up from your long journey.”
“Oh, yeah. Well, I guess I’ll take you up on that.”

And so, we were shown to the rooms Siltvelt had prepared for us. I ended up in a different room from my Father, but since Sakura-chan was assigned to guard him, I put up with it. It seems my Father doesn’t dislike Sakura-chan either. I’m counting on her.
“Ah, Motoyasu-kun.”
While I was resting in the room with Yuki-chan and the others, my Father knocked on the door.
“What’s the matter?”
“Well, you’ve helped me out with all sorts of things, so I thought I’d come by to thank you properly.”
“Why bring it up now? There’s no need for that between you and Motoyasu.”
“Yeah. I know, but… thank you.”
My Father is very polite, isn’t he?
“Also, there are a few things on my mind, so I came by to go over them with you again.”
“Meaning…?”
“Let’s talk inside the room instead of at the door. Sakura-chan, Kou, and Yuki-chan, make sure no one’s eavesdropping.”
“Got it. So, what’s this about?”
“Well, weren’t you targeted for your life because of religious reasons? If that’s the case, I’m wondering if there might be some danger in Siltvelt, too.”

It’s not an impossible scenario. Come to think of it, I recall getting the impression that people in this world have a strange image of heroes. The Three Heroes Church is certainly vile and a heretical sect, but if asked whether other religions are legitimate, I, Motoyasu, wouldn’t know. There are gaps in my knowledge of future events, like holes, and I don’t know what kind of country Siltvelt—which worships the Shield Hero—is.
“I’m sorry, but since I’ve never been to this country in the future, I can’t really say.”
“That’s true. That’s exactly why I think it’s best to stay on guard.”
“I see.”
“How should I put it… Motoyasu tells me all sorts of things, but it seems there are some events I can’t recall unless I ask. So I want to be careful.”
My Father believes the story that he was killed in the past and is doing his best to avoid dying. Given that, the only thing I, Motoyasu, must do is protect my Father with all my might.
“Let’s sort through the likely scenarios. You know how heroes in novels and manga are sometimes given a certain status just to be kept on a leash, right?”
“Are there stories like that?”
“Huh? Ah… Motoyasu, aren’t you one of ‘us’?”

I wonder what he means by “one of us”? Unfortunately, this Motoyasu isn’t very familiar with such topics, except for online games and a few others. “Makai Daichi,” which was all about angel moe, was actually quite excellent even among console games. The reason I ended up playing “Makai Daichi” was that I bought it just because of the cover art. Looking back now, I suppose meeting Filo-tan and Filolial-sama was destined to happen even before I became a hero. I, Motoyasu, am deeply moved by this distant destiny, and my heart is swelling with excitement.
“Motoyasu-kun, I have absolutely no idea what kind of life you led back when you were in modern society…”
“Back when I was in high school, I was always chasing after pigs’ butts.”
“Um… I don’t think we talked about this in much detail before, but weren’t you getting treated terribly by women until you were set straight by Filo, the Filolial I raised?”
“That’s not right. Thanks to Filo-tan, I awakened to true love.”
“Uh, yeah. Um… let’s get back to the topic. So until then, you were living a life where you got along well with pigs, right?”
“That’s right. Looking back, it was a life full of blemishes, but there were all sorts of things that happened.”
“Huh… like what?”

Hmm, examples, you say. I really don’t even want to think about those pigs, but since it’s a request from my Father, I’ll try to recall them. Looking back, the first thing that comes to mind is my junior high and high school years. Back then, my heart was racing with a false sense of happiness. It was…
“Since both my parents were away on business trips overseas, I’d been living alone at my parents’ house almost exclusively since around junior high.”
